# The Cost of Intelligence, Episode 15: The Head of Y Combinator Built AI Memory


### A special on gbrain, Garry Tan’s free memory for AI agents: what his own tests say it saves, and what they say it costs. Plus OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra, and gbrain’s new paid plans.


[Strong Compute](https://substack.com/@strongcompute)


Nov 18, 2026


*Listen to this episode on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/episode/5zE1SKaubE3DTcYlmabSHp) or watch it on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/UXwpl35iXv8) .*


Welcome back to


**The Cost of Intelligence** , our comedy news show about the money behind AI. Each episode, Ben Sand reads the industry’s invoice and asks one question: are you getting more intelligence per dollar?


This week is a special. Most of the show is one open-source project:


**gbrain** , a free shared memory for AI agents, built by Garry Tan, the head of Y Combinator. His own tests say it cuts reranking costs


**60%** , agent calls


**32%** per task, and retrieval


**86%** against pasting the whole chat. They also say making agents check it first costs


**10 to 55% more** per turn. Plus: Tan’s plan to rewrite its search engine in Rust, OpenAI’s


**GPT-6.2 Astra** , and gbrain’s new paid plans. Here’s the written version, with every source linked.


---


## The gbrain special


First, the basics, straight from the repo.


gbrain is a memory layer for AI agents. It’s free, under the MIT license, and Garry Tan wrote it; his README says he built it to run his own agents (


[gbrain on GitHub](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain) ). It keeps your notes, people and companies as plain files and indexes them. Then Claude Code, Codex and other agents search that memory before they answer, instead of starting from zero. It has more than


**33,000 stars** on GitHub. Tan says his own gbrain holds more than


**155,000 pages** . It went public in April.


**The disclosures.** Tan owns gbrain. A paid hosted version carries his name, and its site says it’s backed by Y Combinator (


[gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/) ). So every savings number today is the maker’s own: from Tan’s repos, his changelog and his pull requests, at list prices. We found no measured before-and-after from an outside user. We looked. An audit where the auditee brought the calculator.


A memory tool cuts a bill by sending the model less text. Fewer tokens in, a smaller invoice. Finance calls that math. Engineering calls it a breakthrough.


**But Tan’s own tests also measured the cost of using it.** A one-line rule told agents to check gbrain first. Three agents obeyed in


**30 of 30** turns; without the rule, they checked in


**4 to 6 of 30** . Following the rule cost


**10 to 55% more per turn** , and the pass rate didn’t move. It’s a small test: ten tasks, one run each, from his report dated 7 November (


[the report](https://github.com/garrytan/g-harness-evals/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/2026-11-07-h10-instruction-placement/report.md) ). Checking with the manager before every answer. Every company knows that cost.


On gbrain’s own BEAM 10M test, a plain file-search agent scored


**67.6%** and gbrain scored


**58.9%** . The test can’t tell them apart (


[gbrain-evals](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain-evals) ).


*Per-dollar verdict: it saves money where the maker measured it, and costs money where the maker also measured that.*


---


## The big picture


-


The tracker at


[tokensperday.com](https://tokensperday.com/) starts from a July estimate of


**360 trillion** tokens a day and grows it at its own assumed rate. Grown to 18 November, that’s about


**472 trillion** a day, or about


**57,000 tokens** for every person on Earth.


-


[Epoch AI](https://epoch.ai/data/ai-chip-sales) counts about


**34 million** AI chips sold since 2022, measured in H100 equivalents: five times the count at the end of 2024.


-


The data centers behind them draw about


**30 gigawatts** , our estimate from Epoch’s data center tracker.


-


Last year, AI-focused data centers used about


**half a percent** of the world’s electricity, by our math on


[International Energy Agency](https://www.iea.org/reports/key-questions-on-energy-and-ai) data. That’s about a tenth of a percent of all the energy we use.


-


Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta spent about


**$202 billion** in capital spending last quarter, the bucket that holds data centers and chips, more than double a year ago (company Q3 filings, cash capex).

## The news: Tan’s Rust plan


Tan posted on X early Tuesday that a “GBrain backend engine” will be “written in Rust” and “will replace postgres+pgvector or pglite as the backing store.” He says it’s coming “in the next few weeks.”


[Garry Tan @garrytan Fun project for GBrain coming in the next few weeks using Vorflux as my software factory: GBrain backend engine written in Rust This will replace postgres+pgvector or pglite as the backing store for vector search, graph search, embeddings, RAG and HNSW 6:25 AM · Nov 17, 2026 · 32.6K Views 76 Replies · 15 Reposts · 360 Likes](https://x.com/garrytan/status/2122576951080792543)


That’s a plan, with no cost or speed number and no test. In the next few weeks: the roadmap’s favorite unit of time.


*Per-dollar verdict: a rewrite is a promise. Call us when there’s a receipt.*


---


## The dial


In May, Tan posted that you can “tokenmax $10k/mo” with an agent plus gbrain and get “the AI that everyone will have in 2028 for $100/mo.”


[Garry Tan @garrytan The biggest alpha leak of 2026 is that you can tokenmax $10k/mo with OpenClaw/Hermes + GBrain and get the AI that everyone will have in 2028 for $100/mo, but you can get it now, and that is the biggest single unlock you can have vs your competition 3:31 PM · May 15, 2026 · 895K Views 263 Replies · 298 Reposts · 5.29K Likes](https://x.com/garrytan/status/2055310116325560647)


His own repo sells the same dial. It lists gbrain’s search modes, and at


**10,000 queries a month** on Anthropic’s Sonnet 5.5, the conservative mode’s reading bill is


**$80** and the tokenmax mode’s is


**$400** : gbrain’s own estimate (


[search modes](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/search-modes.md) ). Five times the bill, same project. The gas pedal and the brake, one maker.


*Per-dollar verdict: the dial is yours. So is the invoice.*


---


## GPT-6.2 Astra


OpenAI released


**GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol** on Tuesday. OpenAI says they’re in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and education users, and in the API (


[OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-6-2-astra-sol/) ).


-


Astra’s API costs


**$8 per million input tokens** and


**$40 per million output tokens** ,


**20% below** GPT-6 Astra (


[OpenAI pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) ).


-


OpenAI cites


**Agents’ Last Exam** , a benchmark from Berkeley and Snorkel AI, and says Astra scores


**5.5 points above** Claude Fable 5.2 on it. The


[public leaderboard](https://snorkel.ai/leaderboard/agents-last-exam/) doesn’t list Astra yet, and there, Fable leads on pass rate.


-


OpenAI says Astra did it at


**5% of Fable’s cost** on that test, though the list prices are the same. OpenAI adds that Fable’s results exclude


**nine tasks that used a fallback model** .


-


On


[Epoch’s Capabilities Index](https://epoch.ai/eci) , Astra and Fable 5.2 both show


**174** . Epoch’s raw scores put Astra first, by a hair.


Same sticker, same score, and a launch post that says it’s cheaper.


*Per-dollar verdict: 20% off the old Astra is a receipt. 5% of Fable is a claim.*


---


## Bonus story: gbrain’s hosted plans


gbrain now has a paid hosted version at gbrain.io. Its pricing page lists


**Personal at $49 a month** ,


**Team at $199 a month** with $100 of AI credit every month, and Enterprise at a custom price (


[gbrain pricing](https://gbrain.io/pricing) ). The open-source version stays free to run yourself.


*Per-dollar verdict: free if you run it. $49 a month if someone else does.*


---


## Department of Token Efficiency


Chainsaw fueled. Spreadsheets open. All three cuts are gbrain’s, and all three tests are Tan’s.


**Cut one: the reranker.** A reranker re-sorts search results before the model sees them. gbrain switched its default, for brains that hadn’t picked one, to a cheaper one (


[changelog](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) ).


-


The cost fell from


**$1.51** to


**60 cents** per thousand queries,


**60% cheaper** .


-


It found the right page among its top results for


**298 of 300** questions. The old one found 299.


Sixty percent off, one question lost. A coupon you didn’t have to clip.


**The fine print:** Tan’s own test, one benchmark, at list prices. An earlier trial that cut the candidate list lost at least three questions and was thrown out (


[preregistration](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain-evals/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/2026-10-12-rerank-settings-preregistration.md) ).


**Cut two: the tool menu.** Every turn, an agent rereads its menu of tools. The release cut gbrain’s menu and trimmed its search results (


[pull request](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/pull/5995) ).


-


The menu went from


**13,077 tokens** to


**5,568** .


-


Cost per task fell from


**11.8 cents** to


**8 cents** ,


**32% less** . A team running 1,000 tasks a day saves about


**$38 a day** , our estimate.


A menu you can finally read without a nap. (There’s a goblin. Watch the video.)


**The fine print:** the maker’s test, six models. It finished 454 tasks of 600; before, 441. That gap is within the noise. The saving comes from the whole release: a shorter menu and leaner search results.


**Cut three: retrieval.** On Anthropic’s Sonnet 5.5, pasting a whole chat history cost


**17.3 cents** a question. Retrieving only the relevant pieces cost


**2.4 cents** :


**86% less** . gbrain got


**139 of 150** right; the full paste got 144 (


[benchmark](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain-evals/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/2026-10-07-longmemeval-w10c-full-context.md) ).


Skip the novel. Read the index.


**The fine print:** Tan’s own test, at batch prices. It holds for one question per history. Indexing costs 1.5 cents per history. And the pasted history fit the model’s window.


Ask your CFO if token efficiency is right for you.
